Common questions

Frequently asked questions

What are the requirements for a mutual consent divorce in Chennai?
Under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, the spouses must have lived separately for at least one year, agree that they cannot live together, and settle terms on alimony, stridhan and child custody. A joint First Motion is filed in the Family Court, followed by a Second Motion after the waiting period, which the court may waive in appropriate cases.
When should someone apply for anticipatory bail?
When there is a genuine apprehension of arrest for a non-bailable offence, for example after learning of an FIR or receiving a police notice. The provision is Section 482 BNSS for proceedings under the new codes (earlier Section 438 CrPC).
What are the time limits in a cheque bounce case?
The demand notice must be sent within 30 days of the bank’s return memo. The drawer then has 15 days to pay. If unpaid, the complaint must be filed within one month after that period. Missing a step can end the remedy, so seek advice early.
Where is the office and how do I book a consultation?
The office is in West Mambalam, Chennai. Consultations are by prior appointment so that your matter can be given proper attention. Call +91 98844 41211, message on WhatsApp, or use the form on this page.

Criminal Law

Anticipatory Bail Advocate in Chennai

Pre-arrest bail petitions before the the Court of Session, Chennai and the High Court of Madras.

Section 482 BNSS (formerly Section 438 CrPC)

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Criminal Law
  6. /
  7. Anticipatory Bail Advocate in Chennai

Legal framework and scope

Anticipatory bail is a direction that a person be released on bail if arrested, sought when there is a genuine apprehension of arrest for a non-bailable offence. For proceedings under the new codes it is governed by Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (the successor to Section 438 of the CrPC). Both the Court of Session and the High Court can hear such applications.

Shasti Law Firm prepares petitions that set out the facts, the nature of the dispute, the applicant’s antecedents and willingness to cooperate with the investigation, and appears before the the Court of Session, Chennai and the Criminal Benches of the Madras High Court. The court decides each application on its facts and in its discretion; no outcome can be promised.

Courts typically look at the nature and gravity of the accusation, the applicant’s antecedents, any risk of absconding or tampering with evidence, and whether the accusation appears aimed at causing humiliation. Earlier decisions of the Supreme Court, including Sushila Aggarwal (2020), indicate that protection need not be limited to a fixed period unless the court finds special reasons.

Which code applies?Since 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) have replaced the CrPC, IPC and Indian Evidence Act for new proceedings. Matters already pending, or FIRs registered before that date, may continue under the older codes, so we confirm which code applies at the first consultation.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Copy of the FIR or complaint, if registered and accessible
  • Any police notice or summons, including a notice under Section 35 BNSS (earlier Section 41A CrPC)
  • Government photo ID (Aadhaar, passport or voter ID)
  • Documents bearing on the allegations (agreements, receipts, messages, emails)
  • Any other records identified at the confidential consultation

General procedure

  1. 1Review of the complaint, CSR or FIR and any notice received.
  2. 2Drafting the petition with grounds, and an urgency memo where required.
  3. 3Filing before the Sessions Court or the Madras High Court.
  4. 4Hearing, including the Public Prosecutor’s response.
  5. 5Furnishing bonds and sureties and complying with any conditions if bail is granted.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

Can anticipatory bail be sought before an FIR is registered?
It can be sought when there is a real and specific apprehension of arrest, for example after a police complaint or a notice from the investigating officer. A vague or general fear is usually not enough.
What if the Sessions Court rejects the application?
A fresh application can generally be made before the High Court of Madras. Whether that is advisable depends on the reasons for the rejection.
Does anticipatory bail last until the end of the trial?
Not automatically in every case. As a general position, protection need not be time-limited unless the court gives reasons, but the court can impose conditions and can cancel bail for breach.

Criminal Defence Lawyer in Chennai

Regular bail, default bail, discharge, trial defence and quashing petitions.

BNSS / BNS (formerly CrPC / IPC)

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Criminal Law
  6. /
  7. Criminal Defence Lawyer Chennai

Legal framework and scope

Criminal proceedings affect liberty, reputation and livelihood, and procedure matters at every stage. Shasti Law Firm acts for accused persons in cases under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the older Indian Penal Code for earlier offences, and special penal statutes.

Our work includes regular bail after arrest, default (statutory) bail where the investigation is not completed in time (Section 187(2) BNSS, earlier Section 167(2) CrPC), discharge applications (Sections 250 and 262 BNSS, earlier Sections 227 and 239 CrPC), trial defence and cross-examination, and petitions to the Madras High Court to quash proceedings that amount to an abuse of process (Section 528 BNSS, earlier Section 482 CrPC).

Which code applies?Since 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) have replaced the CrPC, IPC and Indian Evidence Act for new proceedings. Matters already pending, or FIRs registered before that date, may continue under the older codes, so we confirm which code applies at the first consultation.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Arrest memo and remand application
  • Certified copies of the FIR, witness statements (Section 180 BNSS, earlier Section 161 CrPC) and charge sheet
  • Medical records or seizure memos, where relevant
  • Identity and surety documents for the bail bond

General procedure

  1. 1Review of the charge sheet, statements and documents relied on by the prosecution.
  2. 2Bail application before the Magistrate, Sessions Court or High Court as appropriate.
  3. 3Discharge application where the material does not disclose an offence.
  4. 4Trial: framing of charge, evidence, cross-examination and final arguments.
  5. 5Appeal or revision before the Sessions Court or the High Court.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

What is a petition under Section 528 BNSS?
It invokes the High Court’s inherent powers to quash an FIR, charge sheet or proceedings to prevent abuse of the process of court or to secure the ends of justice. It was Section 482 of the CrPC under the older law.
What is default bail?
If the investigation is not completed within the period fixed by law (commonly 60 or 90 days depending on the offence), the accused may be entitled to bail as of right, provided the application is made before the charge sheet is filed.

Cheque Bounce & Section 138 NI Act

Cheque Bounce Advocate in Chennai

Statutory demand notices, complaints and compounding in cheque dishonour matters.

Section 138, Negotiable Instruments Act

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Civil Litigation & Recovery
  6. /
  7. Cheque Bounce Advocate in Chennai

Legal framework and scope

Dishonour of a cheque for insufficient funds, closed account or a similar reason can be an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. Because the remedy depends on strict timelines, the first step is to check the dates on the cheque, the bank return memo and any notice already sent.

We act for payees who need to recover a dishonoured amount and for drawers who need to defend a complaint, for example where the cheque was given as security, was lost or misused, or the claim is time-barred. A private complaint is made to the Magistrate (Section 223 BNSS, earlier Section 200 CrPC), and territorial jurisdiction is determined under Section 142(2) of the NI Act, which generally looks to the branch where the payee holds the account.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Original dishonoured cheque and the bank return memo
  • Copy of the demand notice with postal receipts and delivery tracking
  • Underlying agreement, invoice, loan document or purchase order
  • Bank statements showing the transaction history between the parties

General procedure

  1. 1Present the cheque within its validity period (three months).
  2. 2Send the statutory demand notice within 30 days of receiving the bank’s return memo.
  3. 3The drawer has 15 days from receipt of the notice to pay.
  4. 4If unpaid, file the complaint within one month after that 15-day period ends.
  5. 5Summons, evidence and trial, or settlement under Section 147.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

Can a cheque bounce case be settled?
Yes. Section 147 makes the offence compoundable. Courts may direct payment of costs where compounding is sought at a late stage.
What if the 30-day notice period has been missed?
A complaint based on a notice sent after the statutory period is generally not maintainable, although a civil recovery suit may still be available. Seek advice quickly.

Cheque Bounce & Section 138 NI Act

Section 138 NI Act Lawyer in Chennai

Trial conduct, rebuttal of statutory presumptions and interim compensation.

Sections 138, 139, 143A, 148 NI Act

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Civil Litigation & Recovery
  6. /
  7. Section 138 NI Act Lawyer Chennai

Legal framework and scope

Section 138 trials turn on documents and cross-examination. Under Section 139 the court presumes the cheque was issued for a legally enforceable debt; the presumption can be rebutted by the accused on the standard of preponderance of probabilities, using bank records, accounts, income tax records and the complainant’s own evidence.

We handle trials before the Metropolitan Magistrate Courts in Chennai, applications for interim compensation under Section 143A (up to 20% of the cheque amount), and appeals, where the appellate court may require the appellant to deposit a part of the fine or compensation under Section 148.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Summons received from the Magistrate Court
  • Copy of the complaint and the complainant’s sworn statement
  • Records supporting the defence (proof of payment, stop-payment letters, police complaint for a lost cheque)
  • Bank statements and ledger accounts

General procedure

  1. 1Check whether the complaint is maintainable and filed within time.
  2. 2Plan cross-examination on the complainant’s financial capacity and the alleged debt.
  3. 3Lead defence evidence to rebut the Section 139 presumption.
  4. 4Address any application for interim compensation under Section 143A.
  5. 5Final arguments, judgment, and appeal or revision where needed.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

What is interim compensation under Section 143A?
During the trial the court may direct the drawer to pay the complainant interim compensation of up to 20% of the cheque amount. It is subject to refund with interest if the drawer is acquitted.

Matrimonial & Family Law

Mutual Divorce Lawyer in Chennai

Mutual consent divorce before the Chennai Family Courts.

Section 13B HMA / Section 28 SMA

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Matrimonial & Family Law
  6. /
  7. Mutual Divorce Lawyer in Chennai

Legal framework and scope

Mutual consent divorce is available where both spouses agree that the marriage has broken down and that they cannot live together. It is governed by Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for Hindus, and Section 28 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 for marriages registered under that Act. Other personal laws have their own provisions, which we explain at consultation.

The spouses must have lived separately for at least one year before the petition. A First Motion petition is filed jointly, followed by a Second Motion after the statutory waiting period, which can be moved after six months and not later than eighteen months. In Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017) the Supreme Court held that the six-month period is directory, so the Family Court may waive it in appropriate cases.

A well-drafted settlement covering permanent alimony, return of stridhan, division of assets and child custody and visitation reduces the risk of later disputes. We help both sides understand and record those terms; where spouses’ interests differ, each should consider taking separate advice.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Marriage certificate or registration extract
  • Wedding invitation or photographs as proof of solemnisation
  • Address and ID proofs of both spouses
  • Passport-size photographs of both spouses
  • Written settlement terms on alimony, custody and property

General procedure

  1. 1Joint consultation and drafting of the settlement or memorandum of understanding.
  2. 2First Motion petition before the Family Court, Chennai.
  3. 3Recording of the spouses’ statements and verification of the separation period.
  4. 4Application to waive the waiting period, where the legal conditions are met.
  5. 5Second Motion hearing and grant of the decree.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

Can a spouse living abroad take part by video conference?
Family Courts may permit this on application, subject to the court’s procedure and any documents it requires, such as a properly executed and attested power of attorney.
Is the six-month waiting period always waived?
No. It is directory rather than mandatory, so the court has discretion. Factors include the length of separation, failed reconciliation efforts and whether all settlement terms have been implemented.
Can we file within the first year of marriage?
Section 14 of the Hindu Marriage Act generally bars a divorce petition within one year of marriage, unless the court gives leave for exceptional hardship or depravity.

Matrimonial & Family Law

Family Court Lawyer and Advocate in Chennai

Advice and representation in contested matrimonial petitions, maintenance, child custody and related family proceedings before the Family Courts.

Family Courts Act, 1984

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Matrimonial & Family Law
  6. /
  7. Family Court Advocate Chennai

Legal framework and scope

A family court lawyer advises and represents people in disputes that arise from marriage and family relationships: divorce, maintenance, child custody and visitation, restitution of conjugal rights and proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act. Shasti Law Firm acts in these matters before the Family Courts in Chennai, for either side as the facts require. Consultations are by appointment at the West Mambalam office, and clients from different parts of Chennai and nearby areas can request one.

Family Courts were set up under the Family Courts Act, 1984 to deal with family disputes in a more settlement-oriented way than an ordinary civil court. The Act requires the court to make an effort to help the parties settle, which is why mediation or counselling is commonly directed before a case goes to trial.

Matters include interim maintenance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act and maintenance under Section 144 BNSS (earlier Section 125 CrPC), restitution of conjugal rights, child custody and visitation, guardianship under the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, and proceedings under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. Divorce petitions, both contested and by mutual consent, are also heard by the Family Court.

Which Family Court can hear a case depends on the law and the facts, not on where a lawyer’s office is. For Hindu marriages, Section 19 of the Hindu Marriage Act lists the places where a petition can be presented, including where the marriage was solemnised, where the respondent lives and where the parties last lived together. Other laws have their own rules. The Principal Family Court, Chennai and its Additional Family Courts are listed in the official Chennai court records, and the court and hall for a particular case should be confirmed from the court records when the case is filed.

It is usually sensible to take advice before filing, or soon after receiving a summons or notice, because venue, limitation and interim applications can affect the later steps. A first consultation also helps a person see which of several possible proceedings fits their situation and what each involves.

Which code applies?Since 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) have replaced the CrPC, IPC and Indian Evidence Act for new proceedings. Matters already pending, or FIRs registered before that date, may continue under the older codes, so we confirm which code applies at the first consultation.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Marriage certificate and wedding photographs
  • Addresses of both spouses and details of where they last lived together
  • Birth certificates of children, if applicable
  • Income details: salary slips, income tax returns, bank statements
  • Police complaints, medical records or correspondence relied on
  • Papers from any earlier or pending case between the parties

General procedure

  1. 1Consultation and review of documents, to identify the proceeding and the court that can hear it.
  2. 2Drafting and filing of the petition or counter-statement.
  3. 3Court-referred counselling and mediation.
  4. 4Interim applications for maintenance or child access.
  5. 5Evidence and cross-examination.
  6. 6Judgment, and appeal to the Madras High Court if needed.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

What does a family court lawyer do?
A family court lawyer advises on the available proceedings, prepares the petition or reply, files interim applications, appears at hearings including mediation, and represents the client through evidence and arguments. The lawyer does not decide the outcome, which rests with the court.
When should I consult a family court lawyer?
Ideally before filing a case, or soon after receiving a summons, notice or petition. Early advice helps with venue, limitation and any urgent interim application.
Where are the Family Courts in Chennai?
The Principal Family Court, Chennai and its Additional Family Courts are listed in the official Chennai court records. Their current location, and the court that will hear a particular case, should be confirmed from the official court records or the registry when the case is filed. We confirm the court and hearing date for your case at that stage.
Does the lawyer’s office location decide which court hears my case?
No. The court is determined by the law that applies and the facts of the case, such as where the marriage took place or where the parties lived. A lawyer can appear before a court wherever the office is, but the filing venue must be checked for each case.
How is interim maintenance decided?
Courts look at the income and needs of both spouses, supported by sworn income affidavits and documents, and may fix a monthly amount while the case is pending.
What should I prepare before a consultation?
Bring the marriage certificate, details of children, income and address records, and any court papers, notices or complaints already issued. Please do not send sensitive documents through an unsecured channel.
How long does a family court case take?
There is no fixed period. It depends on the type of case, the court’s calendar, whether the parties settle and how much evidence is involved.

Is pre-institution mediation compulsory?

Criminal Law

Regular Bail Lawyer in Chennai

Bail applications for a person who is already in custody, before the competent Magistrate, Court of Session or the Madras High Court.

Bail after arrest

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Criminal Law
  6. /
  7. Regular Bail Lawyer Chennai

Legal framework and scope

Regular bail is sought by a person who has already been arrested or is in custody, so that they can be released while the case is pending. It is different from anticipatory bail, which is sought before an arrest, and from default (statutory) bail, which arises when the police do not complete the investigation within the time the law allows.

How a bail application is approached depends on whether the offence is bailable or non-bailable, how serious the allegation is, the punishment prescribed, the stage of the case and any special statute involved. Some special laws, such as the NDPS Act, carry their own conditions for bail. The application goes to the court that has the power to hear it for that offence, which may be a Magistrate, the Court of Session or the Madras High Court.

Courts commonly look at the nature and gravity of the accusation, the material collected so far, the applicant’s alleged role, the chance of absconding or interfering with witnesses, any earlier cases and the time already spent in custody. If bail is granted, conditions such as furnishing sureties, surrendering a passport or reporting to a police station at fixed intervals are common. Each application is decided on its own facts and in the court’s discretion, and no result can be promised.

If an application is rejected, the options depend on the order and the reasons given. They can include a fresh application where circumstances have genuinely changed or an application before the higher court. Which course is suitable is a matter for advice on the actual order.

Which code applies?Since 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) have replaced the CrPC, IPC and Indian Evidence Act for new proceedings. Matters already pending, or FIRs registered before that date, may continue under the older codes, so we confirm which code applies at the first consultation.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Copy of the FIR or complaint and the arrest memo
  • Remand order and any custody or production details
  • Earlier bail orders or rejection orders in the same case
  • Charge sheet or final report, if it has been filed
  • Identity and address proof of the applicant and of proposed sureties
  • Details of any other pending cases against the applicant
  • Medical records, if health or age is to be relied on

General procedure

  1. 1Consultation and review of the FIR, remand papers and custody status.
  2. 2Identifying the court that can hear the application and the provisions that apply to the offence.
  3. 3Drafting the application with grounds and supporting documents.
  4. 4Filing, notice to the prosecution and listing before the court.
  5. 5Hearing and arguments; the court passes its order.
  6. 6Compliance with any bail conditions, or review of remedies if the application is rejected.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between regular bail and anticipatory bail?
Regular bail is sought after arrest. Anticipatory bail is sought before arrest by a person who fears being arrested for a non-bailable offence. Different provisions and, often, different courts are involved.
Which court hears a regular bail application?
It depends on the offence and the stage of the case. It can be a Magistrate, the Court of Session or the High Court. The court that has the case, or has the power to hear bail for that offence, is the one to approach.
Is bail available in every case?
No. Bail is generally a right in bailable offences, but in non-bailable offences it is at the court’s discretion, and some special statutes impose stricter conditions.
How long does a bail application take?
There is no fixed time. It depends on the court’s listing, the prosecution’s response and the complexity of the case.

Criminal Law

High Court Criminal Lawyer in Chennai

Quashing petitions, criminal revisions, appeals and bail applications before the High Court of Madras.

Madras High Court

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Criminal Law
  6. /
  7. High Court Criminal Lawyer Chennai

Legal framework and scope

Criminal matters reach the Madras High Court in several ways: as a petition to quash an FIR or proceedings, as an appeal or revision against an order of a lower court, or as an application for bail or anticipatory bail where the law allows the High Court to hear it. The right remedy depends on the stage of the case, the order being challenged and the limitation period.

A petition to quash proceedings is made under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which preserves the High Court’s inherent powers to prevent abuse of the process of any court or to secure the ends of justice. For proceedings under the older code, the equivalent provision was Section 482 of the CrPC. This should not be confused with Section 482 of the BNSS, which is the separate provision on directions for bail to a person apprehending arrest. The two sections have nothing in common apart from the number.

Appeals and revisions are statutory remedies. Whether an order can be appealed or only revised, which court hears it and the time allowed all depend on the order and the law. The High Court may also expect the remedies available before the trial court or the Court of Session to be considered first, so not every grievance is suitable for a High Court petition.

Where the law permits, bail or anticipatory bail may be sought from the High Court directly or after the Court of Session has dealt with the matter. The choice between those routes is made on the facts of the case.

Which code applies?Since 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) have replaced the CrPC, IPC and Indian Evidence Act for new proceedings. Matters already pending, or FIRs registered before that date, may continue under the older codes, so we confirm which code applies at the first consultation.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • FIR, complaint or charge sheet, as relevant
  • The order under challenge, with its date and the court that passed it
  • Filings made before the lower court and any replies received
  • Notices, summons or remand papers
  • A short written chronology of events and dates
  • Details of other proceedings arising from the same facts

General procedure

  1. 1Review of the record and identification of the remedy and the provision that applies.
  2. 2Checking limitation, maintainability and any alternative remedy.
  3. 3Drafting the petition, grounds and affidavit, with certified copies of the impugned order.
  4. 4Filing, numbering and listing before the appropriate bench.
  5. 5Notice to the State or the other side, counter and arguments.
  6. 6Order of the court, followed by compliance or the next remedy.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

What is a petition under Section 528 BNSS?
It invokes the High Court’s inherent powers, for example to ask that an FIR or proceedings be quashed as an abuse of process. It was Section 482 of the CrPC under the earlier law.
Is Section 528 BNSS the same as anticipatory bail?
No. Anticipatory bail is dealt with in Section 482 BNSS. Section 528 concerns the High Court’s inherent powers. They are separate remedies.
Can I come directly to the High Court?
Sometimes, but not always. The law and the High Court’s own practice may require a person to approach the trial court or the Court of Session first. This is decided on the facts.
Does filing a petition stop the case?
Not automatically. Any interim protection is a matter for the court to decide on the application made.

Matrimonial & Family Law

Contested Divorce Lawyer in Chennai

Divorce petitions where the spouses do not agree on separating or on the terms, before the Family Courts in Chennai.

Hindu Marriage Act, 1955

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Matrimonial & Family Law
  6. /
  7. Contested Divorce Lawyer Chennai

Legal framework and scope

A contested divorce is one in which the spouses do not both consent to the divorce or cannot agree on its terms. It is different from a mutual consent divorce, where both spouses join in the petition (see our page on mutual divorce). A contested case goes through pleadings, interim applications, mediation, evidence and arguments, and usually takes longer.

For Hindus, the grounds on which a petition can be presented are set out in Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. They include cruelty, desertion, adultery, conversion, unsoundness of mind and certain other grounds. Other communities are governed by their own personal laws, and marriages under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 have their own provisions. Which law applies, and which grounds are available, depends on the facts. Section 14 of the Hindu Marriage Act generally bars a petition within one year of marriage unless the court gives leave.

The petition is presented in the court that has territorial jurisdiction. Section 19 of the Hindu Marriage Act lists the places where this can be done, which include where the marriage was solemnised, where the respondent lives and where the parties last lived together. For matters in the Chennai area, this will usually mean the Family Courts, Chennai, but the court for a particular case must be confirmed before filing.

While the case is pending, either side can apply for interim maintenance under Section 24 of the Act, and for orders on the custody of children under Section 26. Family Courts are required by law to make an effort at settlement, so mediation or counselling is commonly directed before trial. If the case is not settled, evidence is led and the court decides. An appeal from the decree lies to the High Court in the time the law prescribes. No outcome can be guaranteed.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Marriage certificate and proof of marriage, such as photographs or invitations
  • Proof of address of each spouse and details of where the parties last lived together
  • Details of children, with birth certificates and school records
  • Income and asset details, such as pay slips, returns and bank statements
  • Relevant messages, notices and records of earlier complaints or proceedings
  • Copies of any orders already passed in related cases

General procedure

  1. 1Consultation and review of the facts, the personal law that applies and the grounds that may be available.
  2. 2Checking the court that has territorial jurisdiction and limitation, if any.
  3. 3Drafting the petition or the written statement, with the supporting documents.
  4. 4Interim applications for maintenance, custody or residence, where needed.
  5. 5Mediation or counselling, if the court refers the parties.
  6. 6Evidence, cross-examination and arguments, followed by judgment and, if required, appeal.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

How is a contested divorce different from a mutual consent divorce?
In a mutual consent divorce both spouses agree and file jointly. In a contested divorce one spouse seeks a divorce on grounds that the other may oppose, and the court decides after hearing evidence.
How long does a contested divorce take?
There is no fixed period. It depends on the court’s calendar, whether the parties settle, the number of interim applications and the evidence involved.
Can I get maintenance while the case is going on?
Either spouse can apply for interim maintenance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act where its conditions are met. The court decides on the income and needs shown.
What if my spouse lives abroad or in another city?
The court that can hear the case depends on Section 19 of the Act and on the facts. Jurisdiction should be checked before filing.
Can the case be settled midway?
Yes. Parties can settle at any stage, and the court may record a compromise, including a conversion to a mutual consent petition where the law allows.

Matrimonial & Family Law

Child Custody Lawyer in Chennai

Custody, guardianship and visitation of a child, where the welfare of the child is the court’s main consideration.

Guardians and Wards Act, 1890

  1. Home
  2. /
  3. Practice areas
  4. /
  5. Matrimonial & Family Law
  6. /
  7. Child Custody Lawyer Chennai

Legal framework and scope

Custody disputes arise when parents separate or when there is disagreement about who the child should live with, how the other parent will spend time with the child and who takes decisions about schooling, health and travel. In all of these, courts treat the welfare of the child as the paramount consideration, rather than the wishes or rights of either parent.

Several laws can apply. The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 provides for the appointment of a guardian and for custody orders. For Hindus, the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 deals with natural guardianship, and it provides that the custody of a child under five years should ordinarily be with the mother. Section 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act allows the court to pass orders about children in matrimonial proceedings. Other communities are governed by their own personal laws alongside the Guardians and Wards Act.

Custody can be physical, meaning where the child lives, and legal, meaning who takes major decisions. Courts have recognised arrangements in which both parents stay involved, including shared parenting and structured visitation, where that serves the child. A child who is old enough to form an intelligent preference may be heard, and the court gives that preference weight in the circumstances. Interim orders on custody and visitation are often sought while the main case is pending.

The forum depends on the nature of the proceeding: a Family Court where the matter arises in or alongside matrimonial proceedings, or the court the Guardians and Wards Act designates, and in some urgent situations a petition to the High Court. Court decisions are fact-specific and no particular result can be promised.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Birth certificate of the child and identity details of both parents
  • Orders already passed in any matrimonial, custody or protection proceedings
  • School, medical and daily-routine records of the child
  • Details of each parent’s residence, work schedule and support at home
  • A dated chronology of living arrangements and significant events
  • Passport and travel details, if travel is in issue

General procedure

  1. 1Consultation and review of the child’s circumstances and any existing orders.
  2. 2Identifying the proceeding and the court that can hear the matter.
  3. 3Drafting the petition or reply and any application for interim custody or visitation.
  4. 4Mediation or counselling, where the court directs it.
  5. 5Hearing, and where the court considers it appropriate, an interaction with the child.
  6. 6Final order, with a plan for compliance and for any later modification.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

Does the mother automatically get custody?
No automatic rule applies in every case. For a child below five years, Hindu law says custody should ordinarily be with the mother. Otherwise the court decides on the child’s welfare.
Can the other parent meet the child while the case is pending?
The court can pass interim orders on visitation, including the timing and place. These are decided on the facts and the child’s welfare.
Does the child’s wish matter?
A child old enough to form an intelligent preference may be heard, and the court considers that preference along with other factors.
Can a custody order be changed later?
Orders can be revisited where circumstances change materially, as the child’s welfare remains the guiding consideration.

Maintenance Lawyer in Chennai

Claims for and defence against maintenance, including interim maintenance, for spouses, children and parents.

Section 144 BNSS · HMA · DV Act

  1. Home
  2. /

Legal framework and scope

Maintenance is financial support that one person can be required to pay to another who cannot maintain themselves, such as a spouse, a child or a parent. More than one law provides for it, and the route that fits depends on the relationship, the personal law and the proceedings already pending.

The main routes are these. Section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (earlier Section 125 of the CrPC) allows an application before a Magistrate and applies irrespective of religion. Sections 24 and 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 allow interim and permanent maintenance in matrimonial proceedings, and either the wife or the husband can apply. The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 covers maintenance of wife, children and parents among Hindus, and the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 provides for monetary relief. Other communities have their own personal laws on this subject.

Courts look at the income and needs of both sides, the standard of living, the number of dependants, the assets and liabilities, and the earning capacity of the person claiming. The Supreme Court in Rajnesh v. Neha (2020) laid down that parties in maintenance cases should file affidavits disclosing their income and assets, so complete and accurate financial information matters. Where claims are made under more than one law, courts take the amounts already awarded in one proceeding into account in another.

An order of maintenance can be enforced through the process the law provides, and can be varied where circumstances change. A claim or defence is assessed on its own facts, and no amount or outcome can be promised.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Marriage certificate or proof of the relationship
  • Income proof of both sides, such as pay slips, returns and bank statements
  • Details of expenses, rent, school fees, medical needs and dependants
  • Details of property, investments and liabilities
  • Orders already passed in any related proceedings
  • Proof of any amounts paid so far

General procedure

  1. 1Consultation on the relationship, the proceedings already pending and the route that fits.
  2. 2Preparation of the application or reply and the affidavit of income and assets.
  3. 3Filing before the competent court and service on the other side.
  4. 4Interim order on maintenance, where sought.
  5. 5Evidence and arguments if the matter proceeds.
  6. 6Order and its enforcement, or a later application to vary it.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

Can a husband claim maintenance?
Under Sections 24 and 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, either spouse can apply where the conditions in the Act are met. The court looks at the facts.
Can maintenance be claimed under more than one law?
Claims can be made under different laws, but the courts take amounts already awarded into account, so the claims need to be presented carefully.
How is the amount decided?
There is no fixed formula. Courts look at income, needs, the standard of living, dependants and other circumstances shown by the records.
Why do the court ask for an affidavit of income and assets?
It is meant to put the real financial position before the court. Incomplete or inaccurate disclosure can harm a party’s case.

Civil Litigation & Money Recovery

Civil Litigation Lawyer in Chennai

Civil suits and related applications for property, contract and other private disputes, before the competent civil court.

Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

Legal framework and scope

Civil litigation covers private disputes that are decided by a civil court, as against criminal prosecutions. Common examples are disputes over title to or possession of property, partition among family members, breach of contract, injunctions, declarations and the recovery of money. Recovery of money through summary suits and execution is covered separately on our money recovery page.

Before a suit is filed, three questions usually need an answer. The first is limitation: the Limitation Act, 1963 sets time limits for different kinds of claims, and a suit filed late can be dismissed. The second is the court: the right forum depends on the subject matter, the value of the claim and territorial jurisdiction, and Section 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure deals with where a suit can be filed. The third is whether a statutory notice is required, as it is for suits against the Government under Section 80 of the Code.

A suit moves through pleadings, with a plaint and a written statement, then framing of issues, evidence, arguments and judgment. Interim applications are common along the way, for example for a temporary injunction under Order XXXIX of the Code to preserve the position until trial. The court may also refer parties to mediation or other settlement processes under Section 89 of the Code, and many civil disputes are settled in that way. After a decree, execution proceedings may be needed to enforce it, and appeals lie as the law provides.

If a dispute is between businesses and meets the value and subject tests of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015, it may go to a Commercial Court instead, and pre-institution mediation can be mandatory. This page gives only a general outline, and the correct forum and remedy depend on the facts and documents of each matter. No result can be promised.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Title deeds, sale deeds, patta, encumbrance certificate or other property records
  • Contracts, agreements, quotations and correspondence
  • Notices sent and received, with proof of delivery
  • Payment records, invoices and bank statements
  • Earlier court orders or pending proceedings on the same subject
  • A dated chronology of the dispute

General procedure

  1. 1Consultation and review of the documents, the cause of action and limitation.
  2. 2Deciding the forum and whether a legal notice or pre-suit step is required.
  3. 3Drafting the plaint, with documents and any application for interim relief.
  4. 4Filing, service of summons and the defendant’s written statement.
  5. 5Framing of issues, evidence and cross-examination.
  6. 6Arguments, judgment and, where needed, execution or appeal.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

How long does a civil suit take?
There is no fixed period. It varies with the court’s workload, the issues and the evidence, and many suits are settled before final judgment.
Is a legal notice necessary before filing a suit?
Not in every case. It is required for suits against the Government under Section 80 of the CPC, and it is often sent in other cases to set out the claim and give a chance to settle.
What is limitation?
It is the time within which a claim must be brought. The period depends on the type of claim under the Limitation Act, 1963.
Can a civil dispute be settled out of court?
Yes. The court can refer parties to mediation, and parties can compromise at any stage.

Mutual consent and contested divorce

Legal framework and scope

A divorce lawyer advises on and represents spouses who want to end a marriage, or who have been served with a divorce petition. A divorce is either by mutual consent, where both spouses agree, or contested, where one spouse seeks it and the other does not agree or the terms are disputed. Shasti Law Firm acts in both kinds of matter for clients from Tambaram and nearby areas. Consultations are by appointment at the West Mambalam, Chennai office.

Which law applies depends on the marriage. For Hindus it is the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Marriages registered under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 have their own provisions, and other communities are governed by their own personal laws. The route, the grounds available and the documents needed all follow from that, so identifying the applicable law is the first step at a consultation.

Divorce petitions are usually heard by the Family Court. For a Tambaram resident, where a petition can be filed is a real question, because Tambaram is in the Chengalpattu district and not in Chennai city. The Family Court Lawyer in Tambaram page explains what the official court lists show and how venue is decided. This page concentrates on divorce itself: the two routes, the practical steps, and what to do if you receive a petition.

Mutual consent or contested divorce: which route fits

The choice usually turns on whether both spouses genuinely agree. The two routes differ in how they begin, how much the court has to decide and how long they generally take.

Mutual consent divorce

Both spouses agree that the marriage has broken down and agree on the terms, including alimony, stridhan, property and the children. A joint petition is filed (Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act for Hindus), and the spouses must have lived separately for at least one year before it is presented. There is a statutory waiting period between the First Motion and the Second Motion, which the court can waive in suitable cases. See mutual divorce for the process in detail.

Contested divorce

One spouse petitions on a ground the law recognises, such as cruelty or desertion (Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act), and the other opposes the petition or disputes the terms. The case goes through pleadings, interim applications, counselling or mediation, evidence and arguments. See contested divorce for the grounds and stages.

A case that begins as contested can sometimes be settled midway, and the terms are then recorded as the law allows. The time taken depends on the court, the grounds, how far the parties cooperate and the evidence involved. No result can be promised.

Filing a divorce petition from Tambaram

There is no single answer that applies to every Tambaram resident. For Hindu marriages, Section 19 of the Hindu Marriage Act lists the places where a petition can be presented, including where the marriage was solemnised, where the respondent lives and where the parties last lived together. A Tambaram address is only one of the facts, and the other places connected with the marriage can matter as much.

The official district lists show a Family Court at Chengalpattu and none at Tambaram, and the Chennai City Courts list a Principal Family Court and Additional Family Courts. This page does not say which of them serves a particular Tambaram address. That is confirmed from the court’s notified area and records for each case before anything is filed.

If you have received a divorce petition or notice

A summons or notice normally fixes a date to appear or respond. If it is ignored, the court may go ahead without hearing you, so take advice promptly. If the court that issued it is outside Tambaram, whether it can hear the case is a point to raise early.

  • Note the name of the court, the case number and the date given.
  • Keep the summons, the petition and any proof of how it was served.
  • Do not sign or agree to anything you have not read and understood.
  • Bring everything to the consultation.

Issues decided alongside a divorce

A divorce petition often raises other questions. While it is pending, either spouse can apply for interim maintenance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, and the court can pass orders on the custody of children under Section 26. Permanent alimony, return of stridhan and the division of assets are usually dealt with in the final order or in the settlement. These topics are covered further on the maintenance and child custody pages.

How a consultation works for Tambaram clients

Clients from Tambaram and nearby areas can request a consultation. Consultations are held by appointment at the West Mambalam, Chennai office. At the consultation we:

  • identify which law governs the marriage and whether a mutual consent or a contested petition fits;
  • look at where a petition can be filed, using the facts about the marriage and the spouses’ addresses;
  • go through the documents and note what is missing;
  • explain the steps, and the points on which the other spouse’s position will matter.

Advocate Sharulatha practises before several courts. The court that will hear a particular matter is decided by jurisdiction and is confirmed for your case.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Marriage certificate, or proof of marriage such as photographs or the invitation
  • Details of where and when the marriage took place
  • Current addresses of both spouses and where they last lived together
  • Identity and address proofs of both spouses
  • Birth certificates of children, if applicable
  • Income and asset details: pay slips, returns, bank statements
  • Any summons, petition, notice or earlier order already received
  • For a mutual consent case: the settlement terms, if already agreed

General procedure

  1. 1Consultation to identify the governing law, the route (mutual consent or contested) and where a petition can be filed.
  2. 2Confirmation of the court and its area from court records before filing.
  3. 3Drafting and filing: a joint First Motion petition, or a petition or written statement in a contested case.
  4. 4Counselling or mediation, where the court refers the parties.
  5. 5Interim applications for maintenance or child access, where needed.
  6. 6Second Motion (mutual consent), or evidence, arguments and judgment (contested), and appeal where the law allows.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

Which court hears a divorce case for a Tambaram resident?
It depends on the law and the facts, and not every Tambaram divorce goes to the same court. For Hindu marriages, Section 19 of the Hindu Marriage Act lists the places where a petition can be presented. The correct court is confirmed from the court’s notified area and records before filing.
What is the difference between mutual consent and contested divorce?
In a mutual consent divorce both spouses agree to the divorce and its terms and file a joint petition. In a contested divorce one spouse seeks the divorce on a ground recognised by law and the other opposes it or disputes the terms, so the court decides after hearing both sides.
Do both spouses have to take part in a mutual consent divorce?
Yes. The petition is presented jointly, and the court records the statements of both spouses. Because their interests can differ, each should consider taking separate advice.
How long does a divorce take?
There is no fixed period. A mutual consent divorce is generally quicker because the terms are agreed, but it still involves a waiting period between the two motions, which the court can waive in suitable cases. A contested divorce depends on the grounds, the evidence and the court’s calendar.
What should I do if I receive a divorce petition from a court in another district?
Keep the papers, note the date given and take advice promptly. If you do not respond, the court may proceed without hearing you. Whether that court can hear the case is a point to raise early.
Will maintenance and custody be decided along with the divorce?
While a divorce case is pending, either spouse can apply for interim maintenance, and the court can pass orders on custody of children. Permanent alimony and the division of assets are usually dealt with in the final order or the settlement.
Where are consultations held?
By appointment at our West Mambalam, Chennai office. Clients from Tambaram and nearby areas can request an appointment through the consultation form, by phone or on WhatsApp.

Legal framework and scope

A family court lawyer advises on and represents people in family disputes: divorce, maintenance, child custody and visitation, and proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act. Shasti Law Firm handles these family cases for clients from Saidapet and nearby areas, for either side as the facts require. Consultations are by appointment at the West Mambalam, Chennai office.

People in Saidapet often search for a court by the name of the locality. That works poorly for family cases. The courts listed at Saidapet in the official Chennai court list are Metropolitan Magistrate courts, which are criminal courts, and no family court is listed there. Where a family petition can be filed is decided by the law and the facts of the marriage, not by the area in which you live. This page explains that difference and what to prepare before you take advice.

For descriptions of the Magistrate courts listed at Saidapet, see the Saidapet Courts Guide. For a general overview of family proceedings, see Family Court Lawyer and Advocate in Chennai.

Local court information versus the family-court filing venue

What the Saidapet listing shows

The official Chennai court list (2024) shows several numbered Metropolitan Magistrate courts at Saidapet, including a fast-track court for cheque dishonour cases. It shows no family court at Saidapet. A court being listed in your locality therefore does not tell you where a family case belongs.

Where family petitions are listed

The Chennai City Courts list a Principal Family Court, Chennai and Additional Family Courts. The list does not state their location or how areas or cases are divided among them, and this page does not either. Which of them can hear a particular case is confirmed from the court’s records and notified area before filing.

Why locality alone does not decide it

For Hindu marriages, Section 19 of the Hindu Marriage Act sets out the connecting facts for a petition, such as where the marriage took place, where the respondent lives and where the couple last lived together. A Saidapet address is one fact among them. Maintenance, guardianship and domestic violence proceedings follow their own rules, so the answer can differ from one proceeding to another.

Family cases and criminal complaints from the same dispute

A marriage dispute can lead to more than one kind of proceeding. Petitions for divorce, custody or guardianship are family-court matters. Applications under the Domestic Violence Act go to a Magistrate. A criminal complaint connected with the dispute is dealt with by the criminal courts, under a different procedure and with its own rules on bail.

The proceedings run separately but affect each other. A person named in such a complaint may need advice on anticipatory bail or regular bail as well as on the family case. Whether a particular Magistrate court can hear a given matter depends on the area and the facts, and the Saidapet listing does not say which areas each court covers.

Divorce and related proceedings

Divorce is the most common reason people look for a family lawyer. It can be by mutual consent, where both spouses agree on the divorce and its terms, or contested, where one spouse seeks it on a ground the law recognises and the other opposes. The two routes are explained on the mutual divorce and contested divorce pages. Alongside a divorce, either spouse can ask for interim maintenance and for orders on the custody of children; see maintenance and child custody.

Before you seek advice: what a Saidapet resident can prepare

A short timeline helps an advocate see which proceedings are possible and where they can be filed. It is worth preparing before the consultation.

  • Write down every address each spouse has lived at since the marriage, with dates, and where the couple last lived together.
  • Note where and when the marriage took place, and keep the marriage certificate.
  • Keep any summons, notice, petition or police paper, and note the date and the court named in it.
  • Collect income, bank and property papers if maintenance or alimony may be in issue.
  • List the children’s names, dates of birth, and where they live and study, if custody or visitation is in question.

How to get the filing venue clarified

  • Ask the advocate to check the venue at the first consultation, using your address history and the marriage details.
  • Check the official Chennai City Courts website or the court registry for the current list of family courts, because court lists change.
  • If you have received court papers, note the court named in them and raise any objection to venue early.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a family court in Saidapet?
The official Chennai court list shows Metropolitan Magistrate courts at Saidapet, which are criminal courts, and no family court. Family courts are listed separately under the Chennai City Courts. Court lists can change, so the current position should be confirmed from court records.
Which court hears a family case for a Saidapet resident?
The law and the facts of the case decide it. The Chennai family courts may be among the options, but which court can hear a particular case is confirmed from the court’s notified area and records before filing, and not from the locality alone.
Can a Saidapet resident file a family case outside Chennai?
Sometimes. For Hindu marriages, Section 19 of the Hindu Marriage Act refers to where the marriage took place, where the respondent lives and where the parties last lived together, among other connecting facts. What is the difference between a family case and a criminal complaint from a marriage dispute?
A family case, such as a divorce, maintenance or custody petition, is decided by the family court. A criminal complaint is heard by the criminal courts under a different procedure. Both can arise from the same dispute and can run at the same time, so advice on one should take account of the other.
How do I find out where my case should be filed?
Take your address history and marriage details to an advocate, who can check the venue against the law and the court’s notified area. Court lists change, so the current position is confirmed from court records. Do not rely on the locality name or a pincode.

A timeline of addresses since the marriage, the marriage certificate, details of any children, income and bank records, and any summons, notice or police paper already received.

Legal framework and scope

A domestic violence lawyer advises on and represents people in proceedings under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. Shasti Law Firm acts in these matters for either side as the facts require: for a person who wants to make an application, and for a person who has received one. Consultations are by appointment at the West Mambalam, Chennai office.

Applications under the Domestic Violence Act go to a Magistrate. They are not divorce, custody or guardianship petitions, which are family-court matters, and they are not criminal complaints, which are dealt with by the criminal courts. A single dispute can involve more than one of these, which is why it helps to see the whole situation before deciding what to file or how to reply.

The Act provides for several kinds of relief, including monetary relief. Which of them can be sought, and against whom, depends on the facts and is explained at the consultation. No result can be promised in any case.

If you are in immediate danger, contact the police on 112 first. This page gives general information and is not a substitute for emergency help.

Where Domestic Violence Act proceedings fit among other proceedings

The application before a Magistrate

Applications under the Domestic Violence Act go to a Magistrate. Which Magistrate court can hear a particular application is confirmed from the facts and the court’s records before anything is filed, and not from the name of a locality alone. The Chennai Courts Guide describes the Metropolitan Magistrate courts listed in the Chennai City Courts.

Family-court matters from the same dispute

Petitions for divorce, custody or guardianship are family-court matters and follow their own rules. They are explained on the family court, contested divorce and child custody pages.

Maintenance and monetary relief

More than one law provides for maintenance, and the Domestic Violence Act provides for monetary relief. Where claims are made under more than one law, courts take amounts already awarded in one proceeding into account in another. The routes are compared on the maintenance lawyer page.

Domestic violence applications and criminal complaints

A criminal complaint connected with the dispute is dealt with by the criminal courts, under a different procedure and with its own rules on bail. The proceedings run separately but affect each other.

A person named in a criminal complaint may need advice on anticipatory bail or regular bail as well as on the application under the Domestic Violence Act. Advice on how the two proceedings affect each other is part of the first consultation.

If you have received a notice or summons

A summons or notice normally fixes a date to appear or respond. If it is ignored, the court may go ahead without hearing you.

  • Keep every paper you have received and note the date given and the court named in it.
  • Take advice promptly, before the date, so that a reply can be prepared.
  • Do not sign or agree to anything you have not read and understood.

  • Income and expense details, if monetary relief or maintenance may be in issue.
  • Details of the children, if custody or residence is in question.
  • Any notice, summons, application or earlier order already received, and papers from any other pending case between the parties.

Frequently asked questions

What does a domestic violence lawyer do?
A domestic violence lawyer advises on the proceedings available under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, prepares the application or the reply, and represents the client at hearings. The lawyer does not decide the outcome, which rests with the court.
Which court hears a Domestic Violence Act application?
Applications under the Domestic Violence Act go to a Magistrate. Which Magistrate court can hear a particular application is confirmed from the facts and the court’s records before filing.
Is a Domestic Violence Act application a family court case?
No. Applications under the Act go to a Magistrate. Petitions for divorce, custody or guardianship are family-court matters. Both can arise from the same dispute and can run at the same time.
What is the difference between a domestic violence application and a criminal complaint?
An application under the Act is made to a Magistrate under that Act. A criminal complaint is dealt with by the criminal courts under a different procedure and with its own rules on bail. They run separately but affect each other.
Can maintenance or monetary relief be claimed?
The Domestic Violence Act provides for monetary relief, and other laws provide for maintenance. Courts take amounts already awarded under one law into account under another, so claims need to be presented carefully. See the maintenance lawyer page.
I have received a notice. What should I do?
Keep the papers, note the date given and take advice promptly. If you do not respond, the court may proceed without hearing you.
How long does a case take?
There is no fixed period. It depends on the facts, the court’s calendar and how much evidence is involved.

Which court deals with a criminal case from Tambaram

What the official listing shows

The Chengalpattu district directory lists Judicial Magistrate Courts No. I and No. II at Tambaram. Why the police station matters

The Magistrate court for a criminal case usually follows the investigating police station and the place where the offence is alleged to have happened. A person’s home address in Tambaram is not, by itself, the deciding fact. A case registered in another district, or one taken up by a special agency or a special court, can be heard elsewhere.

What goes beyond the Magistrate court

More serious offences are tried by the Court of Session, and anticipatory bail is a remedy before the Court of Session or the High Court and not before a Magistrate. See Anticipatory Bail Lawyer in Chengalpattu for the Chengalpattu district listing.

If a criminal matter has just arisen

The first days often decide how options are used. These are general points, not advice on your own facts.

  • Get a copy of the FIR or complaint if one is registered, and note the police station, the crime number and the officer named.
  • Read any notice carefully. A notice under Section 35 BNSS (earlier Section 41A CrPC) asks a person to appear and is not the same as an arrest.
  • Do not ignore a summons or notice. Note the date and the court or police station that issued it.
  • Take advice before giving a written statement or signing any paper.
  • If an arrest is feared, ask about anticipatory bail early. If an arrest has happened, ask about regular bail.

Arrest, bail and protection from arrest

Regular bail is sought after an arrest, anticipatory bail before one, and default bail where the investigation is not completed in the time the law allows. Each has its own forum and its own considerations, and the courts decide each application on its facts. See Regular Bail Lawyer in Chennai and Anticipatory Bail Advocate in Chennai. Divorce Lawyer in Alandur

Advice for spouses from Alandur and nearby areas who want a divorce, or who have been served with a divorce petition.

Mutual consent and contested divorce

  1. Home
  2. /

  4. /

Legal framework and scope

A divorce lawyer advises spouses who want to end a marriage, or who have received a divorce petition. Shasti Law Firm acts for clients from Alandur and nearby areas in divorce by mutual consent and in contested divorce. Consultations are by appointment at the West Mambalam, Chennai office. The firm has no office in Alandur.

The question Alandur residents most often face is where the petition goes. The Alandur court complex is listed with civil and Magistrate courts, and the official lists do not show a Family Court there. Alandur is in the Chengalpattu district, where the district directory lists a Family Court at Chengalpattu, while the Chennai City Courts list a Principal Family Court and Additional Family Courts. Which of them is right for a given case depends on the facts and is not something this page decides.

See mutual divorce and contested divorce for the two routes, and the Alandur Courts Guide for what the court lists show.

Where a divorce petition from Alandur can be filed

For Hindu marriages, Section 19 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 lists the places where a petition may be presented. They include where the marriage was solemnised, where the other spouse lives and where the spouses last lived together. Marriages under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 and under other personal laws have provisions of their own.

A current Alandur address is therefore one fact among several. A couple who married elsewhere, or who last lived together in another district, may have more than one possible venue, and the choice can affect convenience and cost for both sides. The Family Court that serves a particular address is confirmed from its notified area and records before filing.

Mutual consent divorce: what the two motions involve

Where both spouses agree, a joint petition is filed. For Hindus this is under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, and the spouses must have lived separately for at least one year before it is presented. The court records the statements of both spouses at the First Motion, and the Second Motion follows after the statutory waiting period, which the court can waive in suitable cases. Terms on alimony, stridhan, property and the children are written into the settlement. Each spouse may wish to take separate advice, because their interests can differ.

Contested divorce

In a contested case one spouse petitions on a ground the law recognises and the other opposes it or disputes the terms. The case moves through pleadings, interim applications, counselling or mediation, evidence and arguments. The time taken depends on the court, the grounds and the evidence, and no result can be promised.

If you have received a notice or summons

A summons normally fixes a date to appear or respond. If it is ignored, the court may go ahead without hearing you. Keep the papers, note the court and the date, and take advice promptly. If the court that issued it seems to be the wrong venue, that is a point to raise early.

Questions that sit alongside a divorce

A divorce case often raises maintenance, child custody and sometimes domestic violence complaints. See maintenance, child custody and domestic violence. These can be dealt with in the same case or in separate proceedings, depending on the facts.

Before you request a consultation

Consultations are held by appointment at the West Mambalam, Chennai office. It helps to have these ready:

  • where and when the marriage took place, and under which law;
  • where each spouse lives now and where you last lived together;
  • whether you and your spouse agree on the terms;
  • any summons, petition or earlier order already received.

The court that will hear a particular matter is decided by jurisdiction and is confirmed for your case.

Documents that may be needed

Requirements depend on the facts of your matter; we confirm the list at the consultation.

  • Marriage certificate or other proof of marriage
  • Date and place of marriage
  • Addresses of both spouses and where they last lived together
  • Identity and address proofs
  • Birth certificates of children, if applicable
  • Income and asset details
  • Any summons, petition, notice or earlier order

General procedure

  1. 1Consultation to identify the governing law and whether a mutual consent or a contested petition fits.
  2. 2Confirmation of where the petition can be filed and which court serves it.
  3. 3Drafting and filing: a joint petition, or a petition or written statement.
  4. 4Counselling or mediation where the court refers the parties, and any interim applications.
  5. 5Second Motion, or evidence, arguments and judgment, and appeal where the law allows.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a Family Court at Alandur?
The official lists show civil and Magistrate courts at the Alandur complex and do not list a Family Court there. The Chengalpattu district directory lists a Family Court at Chengalpattu, and the Chennai City Courts list a Principal Family Court. Which applies to a case is confirmed from the facts.
Where can an Alandur resident file for divorce?
For Hindu marriages, Section 19 of the Hindu Marriage Act lists the possible places, including where the marriage took place and where the spouses last lived together. An Alandur address is only one of the facts.
Can we get a divorce if we both agree?
Yes, through a joint petition for mutual consent, after the spouses have lived separately for at least one year. There is a waiting period between the two motions, which the court can waive in suitable cases.
What if my spouse has filed a petition in another city?
Keep the papers, note the date and take advice promptly. If you do not respond, the court may proceed without hearing you. Whether that court can hear the case is a point to raise early.
Does the firm have an office in Alandur?
No. The firm’s only office is at West Mambalam, Chennai, and consultations are by appointment there.
How long will a divorce take?
There is no fixed period. It depends on the route, the grounds, the court’s calendar and how far the parties cooperate.

Legal framework and scope

A domestic violence lawyer advises on and represents people in proceedings under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. Shasti Law Firm acts in these matters for either side as the facts require: for a person who wants to make an application, and for a person who has received one. Consultations are by appointment at the West Mambalam, Chennai office, and the firm has no office in Tambaram.

If you are in immediate danger, contact the police on 112 first. This page gives general information and is not a substitute for emergency help.

The general explanation of the Act, the kinds of relief and how it differs from divorce and criminal complaints is on the Domestic Violence Lawyer in Chennai page. This page covers what is specific to Tambaram: which court an application from there may go to.

Which court deals with an application from Tambaram

Applications under the Act go to a Magistrate. Tambaram is in the Chengalpattu district and not in Chennai city. The district directory lists Judicial Magistrate Courts No. I and No. II at the Tambaram complex, and a Mahila Court and an Additional Mahila Court at Chengalpattu. It does not list a Mahila Court at Tambaram.

Section 27 of the Act lets an application be made to the Magistrate within whose local limits the aggrieved person lives or works, or the respondent lives, or the cause of action arose. More than one court may therefore be possible, and which is right is decided from the facts. This page does not say which court will take up a particular application. See the Tambaram Courts Guide and the Chengalpattu Courts Guide.

If you want to make an application

An application is prepared from the facts and the documents. A consultation covers what has happened, who the respondent is, where each person lives, what relief is needed and what evidence exists. The Act provides for several kinds of relief, including protection and monetary relief, and which can be sought depends on the case. No result can be promised.

If you have received a notice or application

A notice from the Magistrate fixes a date to appear. Do not ignore it. Keep every paper, note the court and the date, and take advice promptly so that a reply can be prepared in time. Whether the court can hear the application is also a point to check early.

  • Keep the notice, the application and any proof of service.
  • Note the next date and the name of the court.
  • Do not contact the other side in a way that could be read as pressure.
  • Bring all papers to the consultation.

Other proceedings that may run alongside

A single dispute can involve divorce, maintenance, child custody and a criminal complaint as well. Each goes to its own forum. See Divorce Lawyer in Tambaram, maintenance and child custody, and Criminal Lawyer in Tambaram for criminal complaints.

Consultation for clients from Tambaram

Consultations are held by appointment at the West Mambalam, Chennai office. Details are kept confidential, and the court for your matter is decided by jurisdiction and confirmed for your case.

  • Police complaints, medical records or messages relied on
  • Income and expense details, if monetary relief is in issue
  • Birth details of children, if applicable
  • Any notice, application or earlier order already received

General procedure

  1. 1Confidential consultation to understand the facts and any urgent safety concern.
  2. 2Review of documents and identification of the likely Magistrate court.
  3. 3Preparation of an application, or of a reply if a notice has been received.
  4. 4Appearance on the dates fixed and follow-up on interim orders.

This is a general outline. The exact steps, forum and timing vary from case to case.

Which court hears a Domestic Violence Act application from Tambaram?
A Magistrate. Section 27 of the Act allows the application in the court where the aggrieved person lives or works, where the respondent lives, or where the cause of action arose. The district directory lists Judicial Magistrate Courts at Tambaram, but the right court is confirmed from the facts.

Bail Lawyer in Egmore
